question: What did you like most about this prompt?
answer: The 'This computer' section. It gives exact browsers, flags, memory behaviour and honest stand-ins for what the machine lacks (no pad, no touch device, nobody to listen), so I could test the plan's risky ideas instead of guessing. The controller-first UX section was the next most useful: it is specific enough to design from. Linking the real engine kit and hub harness meant I could run a spike and tell builders what actually works.

question: What was confusing?
answer: Three things. First, 'for multiplayer integration into ai-hub as well as for the game on its own': I could not tell whether standalone play must itself have multiplayer or only keep working outside a session, so the plan covers both with solo AI mercs and a same-computer link. Second, most of TASK.md speaks to the builder (title, package, exit interview, chat reply), and only STAGE.md says what the planner does, so I had to work out which lines were mine and which to pass on. Third, the brief says to prefer file:// while the kit's README says ES modules don't load from file://. That only resolves once you try an inline bundle, which does work. A smaller one: 'Music set to 10%' doesn't say which volume it means; I took it as the music channel, not music after the master volume.

question: What was the hardest thing to do?
answer: Scoping. The brief asks for a complete, polished, no-stubs slice of an open-world shooter, with shared-world netcode, attract mode, dev tools and full story, for builders whose capability and budget I don't know. Keeping it original while still capturing what makes the source distinctive took the most thought, and the map-as-plot twist came from that. The other hard part was finding the engine's first-person traps, which its platformer-minded guide doesn't cover: the 160 m far plane, E and Q turning the camera, pointer lock being reset every frame, and the default pad mapping. I found those by reading the minified bundle and running spikes.

question: What would you change in this prompt?
answer: Say plainly which TASK.md lines are for the planner and which are for the builder. Spell out what 'on its own' requires for multiplayer. State the builder's rough budget or capability, so a plan can be scoped to it instead of adding a cut order as a hedge. Add a line to the Sharing section saying planners may use a scratch folder and must delete it afterwards. Note that http.server buffers its port line when piped, because the brief's suggested command hung my script for several minutes. Add to the engine kit's guide a short first-person section covering those traps.
